target.title: Fix stranded menu scroll after a manual refresh clears a provider error
target.body:
Fixes #2046.

## Summary

An explicit refresh can collapse a multi-line provider error while an oversized AppKit menu is being tracked, leaving the viewport stranded below the provider header. This change:

- Arms a one-shot restore only for persistent Refresh/Command-R and scopes it to the initiating menu, tracking session, interaction generation, provider/account selection, and refresh generation.
- Waits for clip/document geometry to settle through the existing event-tracking-aware scheduler, distinguishing AppKit layout corrections from deliberate viewport movement.
- Cancels restoration after scrolling, highlighting or selection changes, child or hosted submenu activity, provider/account switches, close/reopen, cancellation, shutdown, or replacement by a newer refresh.
- Leaves background refreshes untouched and restores observer state during teardown.

The implementation integrates the manual-refresh, menu-session, switcher/submenu, interaction, and shutdown paths. It adds 39 focused viewport tests, adjacent lifecycle coverage, a deterministic root-menu assertion for asynchronous submenu cleanup, and a changelog entry thanking @ss251.

## Verification

- `make check`
- `swift test --filter 'StatusMenu(ViewportRestore|OpenRefresh|PersistentRefresh|SwitcherTracking)Tests'` — 114 tests across 4 suites passed.
- `swift test --filter StatusMenuViewportRestoreTests` — 39 tests passed.
- Hosted-submenu cleanup regression — 30/30 isolated repetitions passed.
- `CODEXBAR_TEST_RETRY_NON_TIMEOUT_FAILURES=0 make test` — 602 selections; all 51 groups passed first attempt with no retries, timeouts, or failures.
- Isolated release build passed.
- Autoreview reported no actionable findings; the final test-only race hardening was independently reviewed.
- A signed debug bundle from the exact candidate passed strict deep signature verification and Gatekeeper assessment. In an isolated deterministic failure-to-success run, one Command-R produced one provider invocation; the same native popup remained open, the error cleared, fresh-update state appeared, and the provider header returned into view without close/reopen.

No authenticated-provider behavior is claimed; live proof used deterministic local responses with credential access disabled. No dependencies changed.

target.title: Add sub2api provider support
target.body:
## Summary

- add a native `sub2api` provider backed by its `/v1/usage` endpoint
- support one labeled group API key per token account, including segmented and stacked multi-account layouts
- render daily, weekly, and monthly subscription quotas, wallet balance, expiry, and named rate-limit windows
- document configuration through the app, environment variables, and `config.json`

## Why

[`sub2api`](https://github.com/Wei-Shaw/sub2api) can expose multiple model groups behind separate API keys. CodexBar did not have a provider that could read those group-scoped quotas, so users had to compare the sub2api dashboard manually.

## Behavior

- reads an HTTPS base URL and group API key from provider settings
- requests `GET /v1/usage?days=30&timezone=<local timezone>` with bearer authentication
- reconciles daily and Monday-based weekly usage from key-scoped daily usage points, avoiding stale subscription counters
- applies a strict 15-second total request deadline
- caches per-account snapshots so segmented account switching keeps the current card visible while refreshing and immediately restores previously fetched groups
- keeps provider identity, widget registration, CLI diagnostics, configuration validation, icon resources, and documentation in sync

## Validation

- `swift test --filter 'Sub2APIUsageFetcherTests|Sub2APIMenuCardModelTests|StatusMenuTokenAccountSwitcherTests'` — 20 tests passed across 3 suites
- `make check` — passed; SwiftFormat reported 0 files requiring formatting and SwiftLint reported 0 violations
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed

The provider was also exercised against a self-hosted sub2api instance with multiple group API keys in segmented layout. No credentials or account data are included in this PR.

## Full-suite note

An earlier full `make test` run reached the existing `AdaptiveRefreshTimerTests` timing-sensitive failure where the manual-mode test observed two completed refreshes instead of one. The sub2api and token-account regression suites pass consistently, including after rebasing onto the latest upstream `main`.

target.title: Bound Codex session metadata reads
target.body:
## Summary

- cap retained Codex session-metadata lines at 256 KiB while indexing local cost-usage JSONL
- drain every 64 KiB `FileHandle` read in its own autorelease pool so discarded chunks do not accumulate
- skip oversized or malformed metadata records, then recover a later valid `session_meta` record
- cover an incrementally written 8 MiB record, the exact 256 KiB boundary, and regenerate the parser hash

## Why

The metadata pre-scan previously appended input until it found a newline. A damaged or exceptionally large JSONL line therefore grew both the explicit line buffer and autoreleased read-chunk storage in proportion to the record size. The scanner now holds at most the configured line limit plus the current fixed-size read chunk and releases discarded chunks promptly.

This is availability hardening adjacent to #1999. It does not establish or claim that report's root cause.

## Validation

- `swift test --filter CostUsageScannerTests` — 16 tests passed
- externally generated 268,435,581-byte JSONL file — later metadata recovered in 2.21 seconds
- `/usr/bin/time -l` on that external-file run — 152,666,112-byte peak RSS, versus 161,497,088 bytes for the ordinary 8 MiB fixture run
- `make check` — passed; SwiftLint reported 0 violations
- `make test` — all 601 selections completed; one unrelated Kimi timing assertion recovered on the built-in retry and its 50-test suite then passed separately without retry
- branch-wide autoreview against current main — no findings, confidence 0.93

target.title: fix: limit Pi cumulative Ultra token overcount
target.body:
Fixes #2037.

## Summary
- reparse changed Pi session files so file-level cumulative usage detection stays stable as logs grow
- group Pi assistant usage samples by provider, model, and turn-like lineage, then convert cumulative-looking monotonic sequences into deltas
- prefer request/message IDs before task IDs so a shared task ID cannot collapse independent requests into one cumulative lineage
- keep samples without a lineage raw, and bump the Pi cost formula fingerprint so old overcounted cache entries rebuild

## Tests
- `swift test --filter PiSessionCostScannerTests` - 20 tests passed
- `make check` - passed; existing missing-translation warnings only
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` - clean
- `make test` - not green locally: `AdaptiveRefreshTimerTests` cancels `menu open advances a long idle timer during refresh without postponing an earlier tick` after 30s before reaching the scanner shard; isolated `swift test --skip-build --no-parallel --filter AdaptiveRefreshTimerTests` reproduces the same failure outside this diff

## Risk
Cumulative detection is guarded to large monotonic sequences where the raw sum is at least 3x the final sample and differs by at least 1M tokens. Ordinary small increasing samples, large monotonic samples without a shared lineage, and large rows with unique request IDs under one task ID remain raw/additive.

Review focus: whether the lineage keys cover the current Ultra fork/replay rows without being too broad for ordinary Pi sessions.
